text:
ashley: Heads-up — seeing tiny pods (~0.1 GPU) get repeatedly evicted during preempt windows in us-west1. Symptoms: short-lived evictions, jobs restart, churn spikes. Putting a short log + describe below. Thinking our preempt-window heuristics + taint affinity are too aggressive for tiny pods.

rajesh: Can you paste the eviction event and the node taint? Curious if it's a strict NoSchedule taint or a soft one.

ashley: Yeah — node has `gpu-preempt=true:NoSchedule`. Pod toleration is only for the Reserved class, not for the warm-pool label. Example eviction event: ```
Warning  Evicted  2m (x3 over 6m)  kubelet  The node had condition: "MemoryPressure" OR preempted for higher priority pods
Annotations: preempt_reason=spot-preempt-window
```
Pod spec snippet: ```yaml
resources:
  limits:
    nvidia.com/gpu: 0.1
tolerations:
  - key: "reserved"
    operator: "Exists"
    effect: "NoSchedule"
```

leo: Got it. This matches an oscillation we've seen where the scheduler treats any preempt taint as immediate eviction target, regardless of pod size. Proposed quick fix: smooth preempt window and add tiny-pod anchoring so pods requesting <0.25 GPU get a grace backoff before eviction scoring. Ran a small sim: evictions ↓ ~62% for tiny pods, overall preempt latency ↑ ~12% (acceptable for batch-ish tiny workloads).

katie: Do we have a metric we can watch in the canary? `tiny_pod_evictions_rate` and `preempt_queue_depth` maybe. Also, can we mark certain namespaces as "anchored" instead of relying on size? That helps product teams opt-in.

leo: Metrics: `scheduler.evictions.count{pod_size=\"tiny\"}`, `scheduler.preempt_window.seconds`. Canary plan: update scheduler configmap to set `preempt_window_smoothing: 30s` and `tiny_pod_anchor_threshold: 0.25` + `tiny_pod_anchor_backoff: 45s`. Also add an opt-in label `inference/anchor: "true"` that namespaces can set.

ashley: Example patch to configmap: ```yaml
data:
  scheduler.yaml: |
    preempt_window_smoothing: "30s"
    tiny_pod_anchor_threshold: "0.25"
    tiny_pod_anchor_backoff: "45s"
    anchor_label: "inference/anchor"
```

ops-bot: Deploy configmap `scheduler-config` updated by ashley via CI at 6166667799 — canary rollout started to 5% of scheduler replicas.

rajesh: If we change smoothing, we might see small increases in spot spillover. What's the cost delta expected? Leo, your sim numbers?

leo: Rough numbers from the cluster sim: cost delta +1.8% on spots during peak, but net savings from reduced restarts + developer support time look positive (hard to quantify). Also reduces churn which saves scheduling cycles — small perf win overall.

katie: I'll run the canary in us-west1 for 2 hours and monitor `tiny_pod_evictions_rate`, pod restart counts, and customer impact dashboards. If we see any regression, we revert configmap and force rollout. Revert command: `kubectl rollout restart ds/scheduler -n infra && kubectl apply -f scheduler-config-backup.yaml`.

ashley: Thanks — I'll coordinate with oncall. If canary looks good, plan to roll to 50% next day and then full. Also will draft short note for customers using reserved taints so they know about slightly longer preempt windows for ultra-small pods.

rajesh: One ask — add unit tests in scheduler sim for mixed-size eviction prioritization. We keep hitting edgecases when we tweak heuristics.

leo: Agree. I'll add a regression test. Also logging: add a label to eviction events `eviction_policy=tiny-anchor-v1` so we can filter.

katie: Canary started. I'll report back in ~2h. :eyes: 

ashley: TY all. Hoping this kills the tiny-pod thrash without materially raising costs. :crossed_fingers:
